document.title: U.S. Embassy Kabul Cable 003863, "Afghanistan: Where We Stand and What We Need"
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan 20/20: The 20-Year War in 20 Documents | National Security Archive
document.note: [Secret] Neumann warns 'we are not winning in Afghanistan; although we are far from losing.' He cites a lack of resources and growing Taliban offensives, and urges equipping Afghan forces, taking out Taliban leadership in Pakistan, and investing in infrastructure.

persons.name: Ronald E. Neumann
persons.role: U.S. Ambassador to Afghanistan, author of the cable

mentions.quote: Classified By: Ambassador Ronald E. Neumann for reasons 1.4 (B) and (D)
A year after I arrived the overall military situation has worsened in the south.
We need to use President Karzai's September 26 visit to Washington as an important milestone
President Karzai has promised me a change from the current corrupt and ineffective governor.
Presidents Karzai and Musharraf to meet

persons.name: Rangin Dadfar Spanta
persons.role: Afghan National Security Advisor (cable names 'NSA Rassoul'), visited Pakistani counterpart
persons.status_detail: Identification uncertain; the cable says only 'NSA Rassoul'. Zalmai Rassoul was the Afghan NSA in 2006.

mentions.quote: NSA Rassoul recently visited his Pakistani counterpart (Aziz)

persons.name: Tariq Aziz
persons.role: Pakistani national security counterpart to the Afghan NSA

mentions.quote: NSA Rassoul recently visited his Pakistani counterpart (Aziz)
both sides seem ready for Presidents Karzai and Musharraf to meet

events.description: Ambassador Neumann sends cable assessing that the U.S. is not winning in Afghanistan and requesting resources.
Expected Taliban offensive; the size of the forces employed surprised coalition planners.
Operation Mountain Thrust bought time, particularly in Oruzgan.
Planned Karzai visit to Washington, to be used to announce new programs for Afghan security forces and road building.
Afghan NSA Rassoul visited his Pakistani counterpart Aziz, laying the groundwork for a Karzai-Musharraf meeting.
Ambassador Neumann's cable recommends roughly $600 million in supplemental funding, supports a Karzai-Musharraf initiative, and concludes 'We are not losing' but are too slow.
The GOA and ISAF, with U.S. support, examine fielding more local auxiliary police at provincial levels to fill the security gap until the ANP is ready.
A planned visit by President Karzai to Washington/the U.S. is flagged as the moment to announce new funds and visions for Afghan forces.
Ambassador Neumann sends cable assessing that the US is not winning in Afghanistan and requesting more resources.
Planned visit of President Karzai to Washington, to be used to announce new programs for equipping Afghan forces and road building.
Taliban offensive in southern Afghanistan, larger than predicted, with surprising numbers of insurgents.
Mountain Thrust operation bought time, particularly in Oruzgan.
Afghan NSA visited his Pakistani counterpart Aziz.

key_claims: The U.S. Ambassador states that the U.S. and NATO are not winning in Afghanistan, though not losing.
The 2006 Taliban offensive was far larger than anticipated and expanded Taliban control over the rural population in the south.
The Taliban leadership is secure in Pakistan, and the cable urges real Pakistani progress in taking out that leadership.
The south (Kandahar, Helmand, Oruzgan) deteriorated sharply while the east improved through military action, roads and better governors.
The cable requests $600 million for roads linking district and provincial capitals, which it treats as a security measure.
Afghan forces, especially the police, are inadequate, and local auxiliary police are being considered as a stopgap.
